speaker: Phil Hufford
words: Yes, well, it was very, yeah, it was fairly peculiar. We were working together. What happened was that the Denver Region Greens decided that it was important to notify the public about the hazards, the dangers to protesters attending the Encirclement at the Rocky Flats plant, and so we put together a news release, which had several different groups on it, and those... Yes, and that was, yeah, that was not the, the original one by any means, and Paula and Sue Hurst were on the original one. There we were working well together on that, in fact, Paula wanted to add material to the original news release, which was a little bit longer than the one you see, and I was trying to convince her that we needed to keep it short, and I had set a tentative day to have a news conference on this, and I had discussed this, actually, the date, there's a couple of different days that got mentioned in there, and I had discussed with Paula and Sue and Dr. Nichols, possibly having the news conference on the 18th of July, and then I began to realize that that was not going to be possible, and I tentatively reschedule. This was very tentative at the time. I then I rescheduled it tentatively for Wednesday the 19th, and it turns out that I wasn't able to get everybody's approval on the news release by that time, but we were all working together on this, is very cooperative, and then something happened on the 18th, which is a Tuesday. Paula and Sue turned up at a news conference that the National Toxics Campaign, Adrienne Anderson and a variety of other groups, Coperg and Clean, what is it, Clean Water, or some other group, and there was somebody else in there, I forget who this was, because I was not at the news conference, but it was on chlorofluorocarbon impacts on the atmosphere, and basically was about the destruction of the ozone layer and impacts on the greenhouse effect. Well, Paula and Sue showed up just minutes before this news conference was to happen. I did happen to videotape the news conference, and I saw Paula standing there, so I mean, I thought she was there, but she also told me about this, and I also was told about it by Adrienne. I was not there myself, so anything regarding what was said there, of course, is some type of hearsay, but I did get a description from both sides, and Sue and Paula felt a couple of things. They first of all, they felt that they were being snubbed by Adrienne because Adrienne had sent this, is what they claimed, and I later, later learned this was not the case, but they claimed that Adrienne had sent an invitation to a little get together with a person from Fernald, Ohio, called Lisa Crawford, who was coming out to speak later that week. She was speaking in Arvada on the 22nd of July, Saturday the 22nd So, on the 21st she was flying into town, and there was going to be a little low party for people to meet her at the office that Adrienne uses and also shares with Colorado Peace Network, and they claim, excuse me, they claim that Adrienne had scribbled a handwritten invitation on the back of a notice of Lisa Crawford's talk to a person in Fort Collins named Joan Seaman, who's with the group Committee against radio toxic pollution, and subsequently I did speak with Joan Seaman about this, and she did get something with a handwritten invitation on it, but it was mailed from Boulder, and she had no idea if it was Adrienne's handwriting, and Adrienne said she never had written this thing. In fact, Adrian didn't have anything to do with organizing this little get-together with Lisa Crawford, and I had heard about it because I'd heard about it beforehand because I had attended a Rocky Flats Alliance meeting a week before, where it was announced and everyone was invited that was in attendance at that meeting to come and meet Lisa Crawford, and this was the same group that Paula and Sue had walked out on in some disgust over some issue or other, and seemed to have stormed out of a meeting there, saying they didn't want to have anything to do with the Rocky Flats Alliance, so they weren't there to get the general invitation. Well, anyway, that was one accusation they made to Adrienne. The other was that she had purposely scheduled her news conference to somehow sabotage this other news conference that had really never been scheduled for Tuesday, you know, I mean, there were only four people that knew that that of that time period, that Tuesday date, and that was Paula, Sue, Harvey Nichols, and myself. And then I changed the date and moved it to Wednesday, and somehow Paula and Sue didn't seem to understand that had been changed, and I spoke with them subsequently, and I said, "Well, gee, Paula, you know you're really just wrong on this one. Adrienne never even knew that it was scheduled on Tuesday, and here you are accusing her of sabotaging this news conference that she never even knew was scheduled," and they, they just kind of tenaciously have stuck with that interpretation. I mean, I've, I've corrected them three or four different times, I've told them they were wrong, because I hear them saying they. Same story to people subsequently, and I'd say "no, you know, this is not right," and yet they'd still stick with that, so I don't really know what happened there, they, they seem to be making some, some allegations about I'm not sure if it was Adrienne herself or her organization. Okay, they seem to be making some allegations about either Adrienne's activities or the activities of the National Toxics Campaign, of which I considered fairly ridiculous allegations, and didn't pay any attention to them.

Tom Row of the American Friends Service Committee offered his good offices to act as a mediator, and Paula and Sue refused to meet with Adrienne with Tom Row there as a mediator, they have become rather intransigent when it comes to Adrienne Anderson, and in fact they had their name removed from our news release, if you'll notice, because it had Adrienne Anderson's name on it, and...

speaker: Phil Hufford
words: Well, I have. I mean, I've spoken with some of the union people who are behind the Superfund idea. They were at this little gathering the evening welcoming meeting for Lisa Crawford, and when they were talking about the Superfund for workers, I said, "well, that sounds great, but that should be part of a Superfund for victims, and that all victims of contamination should be somehow compensated for their losses, be they property values or health effects in that workers should be considered as victims in this, and it shouldn't be targeted specifically at workers." But there's another thing about this, when you, when you decommission or go into an economic conversion of a plant like Rocky Flats, if you were to suddenly phase out 2,500, 3,000 or 5,000 jobs that would have a devastating effect on local economy and that is an important factor that needs to be addressed. There, there should not be a precipitous cut off of funds in terms of wages, and there are all these other issues surrounding the cleanup of that plant, the decontamination of the soil, and all of that as well. Some people can be shifted to those jobs, but just the economic impact on the local community should be taken into account, and that is where the idea of a super fund for victims and factoring the workers in as victims I think is an excellent idea, and Denver certainly has gotten its share of contamination relative to other cities. I mean, there's no other place in the world that I'm aware of now. There might be some in the Soviet Union squirreled away somewhere, but at least in the Western world that I'm aware of, there is no domestic water supply contaminated with plutonium, except here. Now, that is highly unusual, and the people of Broomfield were left to twist slowly in the wind when the tritium contamination took place in '73. The people of the Denver metropolitan area have suffered tremendous exposure and are still exposed to contamination unheard of anywhere else in the country, and perhaps in the world, and we deserve some kind of help, federal help, compensation, or whatever, and a super fund for victims and for workers is wholly justifiable just on those grounds, in my opinion.
